card.summary: 1 GB attachment storage per base on Free, with unlimited bases and 1,500 bases per workspace

free_tier.stated: 1 GB attachment storage per base on Free, with unlimited bases and 1,500 bases per workspace

egress.terms: Free; attachments served from airtableusercontent.com (CloudFront-fronted) with expiring signed URLs

record.tooling: Official Web API v0: POST /v0/{baseId}/{recordId}/{attachmentFieldId}/uploadAttachment accepts raw bytes up to 5 MB, larger files go via the content.airtable.com upload-then-attach flow
record.chaining: 1 GB x 1,500 bases x N workspaces = ~1.5 TB per free workspace as documented, multiplied by unlimited free workspaces. Pricing config also states 'unlimited bases' on Free; the 1,500 figure is the per-workspace cap. This is the single largest documented multiplicative figure in this area.
record.limits_note: 1,000 records per base on Free; 5 MB per direct API upload; 1,000 API calls per workspace per MONTH on Free; only 5 editor/creator collaborators; 1 GB per base is the billing-flag field maxTotalAttachmentSizeInBytes=1000000000
record.reliability_note: 1,000 API calls per month on Free is a hard wall - that is ~33 uploads/day, so the 1.5 TB chain is rate-limited long before it is capacity-limited.

evidence.proved: 'How many bases can a single workspace store? 1500 Bases per workspace'; also '1000 records per base... 1GB per of attachment storage per base' for the Free tier

(raw page JSON) - Free plan object: maxTotalAttachmentSizeInBytes=1000000000, maxRowsPerApplication=1000, 'descriptionMarkdown: Unlimited bases / 1,000 records per base / 1GB attachment space per base'; Enterprise: maxTotalAttachmentSizeInBytes=1000000000000 (1 TB/base)
'Upload an attachment up to 5 MB to an attachment cell via the file bytes directly'
